title: Who is the Worst NBA MVP ever?
text:
Every year, the NBA’s Most Valuable Player award goes to the player who performs the best during the regular season. However, not all MVP seasons are equal. Some players load up the stat sheet with elite efficiency, while others win the award with underwhelming seasons compared to the rest.
To find the worst MVP of all time, I looked at every MVP season since 1955 through Win Shares per 48 minutes (WS/48). This is one of the main used measures of efficiency and overall value.
The following charts break down how MVPs performed in scoring compared to efficiency, who the lowest-rated MVPs are, and how they stand out historically.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)

mvp <- read_csv("nba_mvp_seasons_1955_2025.csv")

worst <- mvp %>% slice_min(WS_per_48, n = 1)

ggplot(mvp, aes(x = PTS, y = WS_per_48)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey60", size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = worst, aes(x = PTS, y = WS_per_48), 
             color = "red", size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = worst,
    aes(label = paste0(Player, " (", Season, ")")),
    color = "red", size = 4, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "MVP Scoring vs Efficiency (WS/48)",
    subtitle = "Red point = Worst MVP season by efficiency\n(WS/48; lower is worse)",
    x = "Points Per Game",
    y = "Win Shares per 48 Minutes"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12)
  )









The first graph compares MVPs scoring to their WS/48 efficiency. This shows that points alone don’t make an MVP season. Most MVPs sit at high efficiency levels while the worst MVP is far below the rest of the field. Even when that MVP had a good scoring output, their efficiency was way below what we would expect from an MVP.
This chart makes a clear point. The worst MVP was not a bad scorer, they were just historically inefficient.
Now that we can see how the worst MVP compares to the others, the next thing to do is find and rank the worst MVP seasons. This will allow us to see if the worst MVP season is an outlier or if it is part of a group of weaker MVPs.


Code
worst10 <- mvp %>% 
  arrange(WS_per_48) %>% 
  slice(1:10) %>% 
  mutate(Player_Season = paste0(Player, " (", Season, ")"),
         Player_Season = fct_reorder(Player_Season, WS_per_48))

ggplot(worst10, aes(x = Player_Season, y = WS_per_48)) +
  geom_col(fill = "firebrick") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(WS_per_48, 3)), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "The 10 Worst MVP Seasons in NBA History",
    subtitle = "Ranked by Win Shares per 48 (lower = worse)",
    x = "",
    y = "WS/48"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
  )









The bar chart of the 10 worst MVP seasons shows a clear look of who is at the bottom of list. The lowest WS/48 belongs to the worst MVP season ever. The gap between Dave Cowens and the players above him show how unusual it is for an MVP award winner.
This ranking gives a clear answer to the main question which is “Who is the worst MVP in NBA history?”
The graph points to Dave Cowens 1972-73 season that definitely under performed the others.
Identifying the worst MVP however, is not enough. It is key to know when the season occurred and how that fits into the rest of NBA history. Was it regular in that era? Was efficiency lower around the league at the time? Or is it actually a year that stands out?


Code
ggplot(mvp, aes(x = Season, y = WS_per_48, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "grey50", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = worst, aes(x = Season, y = WS_per_48),
             color = "red", size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = worst,
    aes(label = paste(Player, "\n", Season)),
    color = "red",
    size = 4,
    nudge_y = .02
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "MVP Efficiency Over Time (1955–2025)",
    subtitle = "Dave Cowen’s 1972–73 MVP season stands out as the least efficient",
    x = "Season",
    y = "WS/48"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12)
  )









The line chart follows MVP efficiency from 1955 to 2025. Even across 70 years, through rule adjustments, style changes, and different paces, one point is below the rest. That is the worst MVP season of all time.
Seeing this data across the rest of the NBA MVPs, it reinforces the conclusion. Dave Cowens 1972-73 season is the worst MVP season ever.

title: 2014 Vanderbilt is the Worst Team to Win the College World Series Statistically
text:
Omaha has seen 76 teams win a championship at Rosenblatt and TD Ameritrade stadiums since the inaugural College World Series in 1947. I have always been curious about who the worst team to ever win the tournament was statistically.
When I initially started this project, I assumed that the worst CWS champion ever would be a team in the wooden bat era of college. Metal bats were not allowed in college baseball until the 1974 season. The bats were weakend in 2012 and offensive numbers in college saw a steep drop while defensive stats saw an improvement in areas like ERA.
Throughout the process of making this blog, I had just one question. Who is the worst statistical team to ever win the College World Series?
In compiling all of my data and making charts for different categories, I have determined that the 2014 season saw the worst College World Series champion ever. That team being the Vanderbilt Commodores.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)


## == 1. LOAD & PREP DATA ==

batting  <- read_csv("cwsbatting.csv")
pitching <- read_csv("cwsfielding.csv")

cws <- batting %>%
  select(
    Year,
    Team,
    W.L = `W-L`,
    R,          # runs scored
    BA
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    pitching %>%
      select(
        Year,
        Team,
        W.L = `W-L`,
        ERA,
        R_allowed = R   
      ),
    by = c("Year", "Team", "W.L")
  ) %>%
  
  drop_na(ERA, R_allowed) %>%
  
  mutate(
    Wins   = as.numeric(sub("-.*", "", W.L)),
    Losses = as.numeric(sub(".*-", "", W.L)),
    Games  = Wins + Losses,
    R_per_game  = R / Games,
    RA_per_game = R_allowed / Games
  )


cws <- cws %>%
  mutate(
    offense_rank  = rank(R_per_game),   
    pitching_rank = rank(-ERA),         
    worst_score   = offense_rank + pitching_rank
  )

worst_row <- cws %>%
  arrange(worst_score) %>%
  slice(1)

worst_team <- worst_row$Team[1]
worst_year <- worst_row$Year[1]


cws <- cws %>%
  mutate(
    is_worst = Team == worst_team & Year == worst_year
  )


## == 2. PLOT 1: SCATTER (OFFENSE VS PITCHING) ==

p1 <- ggplot(cws, aes(x = ERA, y = R_per_game)) +
  
  
  geom_point(aes(color = is_worst), alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  
  
  geom_text_repel(
    data = cws %>% filter(!is_worst),
    aes(label = Team),
    size = 2,
    color = "grey20",
    max.overlaps = 200,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
 
  geom_text_repel(
    data = cws %>% filter(is_worst),
    aes(label = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")")),
    size = 3,
    color = "red",
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = "red", `FALSE` = "grey70"),
    labels = c(`TRUE` = "Worst champion", `FALSE` = "Other champions")
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "CWS Champions: Offense vs Pitching",
    x = "ERA (higher = worse pitching)",
    y = "Runs scored per game (lower = worse offense)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

p1









Now, this chart shows every champion teams ERA and runs scored per game. You’ll notice Vanderbilt in 2014 is highlighted red. However, just this chart alone does not tell the whole story.


Code
## == 3. PLOT 2: OVERALL WORSTNESS BAR CHART ==

cws_bar <- cws %>%
  arrange(worst_score) %>%
  
  slice(1:10) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")"))

p2 <- ggplot(cws_bar,
             aes(x = reorder(label, worst_score),
                 y = worst_score,
                 fill = is_worst)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = "red", `FALSE` = "black"),
    labels = c(`TRUE` = "Worst champion", `FALSE` = "Other champions")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Worst College World Series Champions",
    subtitle = "(Hitting + Pitching)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Combined rank (lower = worse)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

p2









Above is the chart that shows the bottom 10 statistical champions. The combined rank takes the worst teams ERA and runs scored per game and adds them together. The following two graphs help tie it all together.


Code
## == 4. PLOT 3: RUNS PER GAME OVER TIME ==

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(grid)   

best5_runs <- cws %>%
  arrange(desc(R_per_game)) %>%
  slice(1:5)

worst5_runs <- cws %>%
  arrange(R_per_game) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  filter(!is_worst)  

vandy <- cws %>% filter(is_worst)

p3 <- ggplot(cws, aes(x = Year, y = R_per_game)) +
 
  geom_line(alpha = 0.25, color = "grey80") +
  geom_point(color = "grey80", size = 1.8) +

  geom_point(data = best5_runs, color = "darkgreen", size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = worst5_runs, color = "purple", size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = vandy, color = "red", size = 3.2) +

  geom_text_repel(
    data = best5_runs,
    aes(label = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")")),
    color = "darkgreen",
    size = 2.5,
    nudge_y = 0.4,
    direction = "y",
    box.padding   = 0.15,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    segment.size  = 0.4,
    segment.color = "darkgreen",
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.01, "npc")),
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(
    data = worst5_runs,
    aes(label = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")")),
    color = "purple",
    size = 2.5,
    nudge_y = -0.4,
    direction = "y",
    box.padding   = 0.15,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    segment.size  = 0.4,
    segment.color = "purple",
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.01, "npc")),
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(
    data = vandy,
    aes(label = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")")),
    color = "red",
    size = 2.5,
    nudge_y = 0.5,
    direction = "y",
    box.padding   = 0.15,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    segment.size  = 0.4,
    segment.color = "red",
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.01, "npc")),
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Runs per Game by CWS Champions",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Runs scored per game"
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.2))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

p3









As you can see, Vanderbilt has the seventh worst runs scored per game out of any CWS champion ever. However, just the runs scored per game ranking alone can not tell us that this Vanderbilt team was the worst championship team ever.


Code
## == 5. PLOT 4: ERA OVER TIME ==

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)

best5  <- cws %>% arrange(ERA) %>% slice(1:5)

worst5 <- cws %>% 
  arrange(desc(ERA)) %>% 
  slice(1:5) %>% 
 
  filter(!is_worst)

p4 <- ggplot(cws, aes(x = Year, y = ERA)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 2) +

  
  geom_point(
    data = cws %>% filter(is_worst),
    aes(x = Year, y = ERA),
    color = "red",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = cws %>% filter(is_worst),
    aes(label = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")")),
    color = "red",
    size = 3,
    nudge_y = 0.25,
    direction = "y",
    segment.color = NA
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(
    data = best5,
    aes(label = Team),
    color = "darkgreen",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = worst5,
    aes(label = Team),
    color = "purple",
    size = 3
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "ERA of CWS Champions",
    x = "Year",
    y = "ERA (lower is better pitching)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

p4









To find the worst team to ever win the College World Series we must also look at the ERA of each team. As you can see in the chart above, it shows that Vanderbilt had the third highest ERA of any champion ever. Now that we can see the runs scored per game and the ERA of each team, we can safely say 2014 Vanderbilt was not a very good statistical team. To really drive home the point of 2014 having the worst champion, I had to use Vanderbilt’s ERA and runs scored per game to find their average run differential per game.


Code
cws <- cws %>%
  mutate(run_diff = R_per_game - RA_per_game)

df_worst10 <- cws %>%
  arrange(run_diff) %>%          
  slice(1:10) %>%               
  mutate(
    label    = paste0(Team, " (", Year, ")"),
    is_worst = Team == worst_team & Year == worst_year
  )

p_diff <- ggplot(df_worst10,
                 aes(x = run_diff,
                     y = reorder(label, run_diff),
                     fill = is_worst)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "black"),
    labels = c("FALSE" = "Other Champions",
               "TRUE"  = "Worst Champion"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Run Differential per Game (R/G − RA/G)",
    subtitle = "10 weakest College World Series champions by run differential",
    x        = "Run differential per game",
    y        = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9)  
  )

p_diff









As you can see from the bottom 10 champions ever, Vanderbilt in 2014 had a negative run differential per game. They are the only team to ever have a negative run differential per game and still win the College World Series. This leads me to say and confirm that Vanderbilt in 2014 is the worst team ever statistically to leave Omaha with the championship trophy.
